messages.subject: Modeling 3D Point Process in INLA
parts:
Has anyone had any experience using ILA to model 3D cartesian points? Could not find much on the internet. If someone could point me in the right direction that would be great.

Thanks.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Modeling 3D Point Process in INLA
parts:
Hi,

the principle would be the same as for 2D fields, but there is less
direct support for 3D point processes and fields at the moment.
For SPDE/Matern fields in 3D, you can try the experimental
https://github.com/finnlindgren/inlamesh3d package, that takes a given
tetrahedralization (e.g. from delaunayn() on a regular 3D lattice) and
creates a mesh object that can be used with special the special
version of inla.spde2.matern(). It also has an inla.spde.make.A()
function that can be used in the same way as for 2D meshes.
One can use that to construct the point process likelihood in
essentially the same way as for 2D.

The 3D support will be merged into INLA and the upcoming fmesher
package; until then, it's experimental and you'll need to "know what
you're doing" to use it...

Finn
